title: Content-addressed prefix fragment store with soft references and batch-aware eviction
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During peak workloads we observe substantial redundant KV cache entries for shared prefixes across different requests and sessions. Redundancy increases GPU memory pressure and causes batch fragmentation when the scheduler assembles per-request KV backings. Existing prefix-coalescing heuristics reduce duplicates but still store per-request copies in pinned GPU buffers.

Proposal: Implement a content-addressed fragment store for prefix KV slices: compute stable fingerprints (SHA256 short hash) for contiguous KV 'fragments' extracted from decoded prompts and store a single canonical GPU-resident fragment per fingerprint. Use a lightweight bloom-filter index on the CPU side to quickly determine likely hits without costly lookups. Maintain soft reference counts and last-used timestamps; when a batch needs a prefix, the runtime will map pointers to the canonical fragment instead of copying bytes. Eviction is batch-aware: fragments with low reuse probability are scheduled for eviction during off-peak or in between large batches to avoid disrupting steady-state throughput.

Goals: reduce duplicate memory for common prefixes, avoid CPU->GPU memcpy for already materialized fragments, and keep tail-latency regressions under 1ms while improving overall throughput and memory efficiency.

Why unique: this approach is content-addressed (CID-like) and exposes reference semantics suitable for concurrent batches, differing from prior per-request dedupe heuristics by providing a canonical shared store and explicit soft references that integrate with the batcher and the scheduler.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical fragment store implemented and integrated with KV manager
Bloom-filter index prevents >95% of false-negative cache hits on common prefixes in our 30-day traffic sample
End-to-end tests show no >1ms increase in median P99 generation latency compared to baseline when store is enabled
Measured duplicate KV footprint reduced by >=60% on the benchmarks derived from customer workloads (chat & code completion traces)
Graceful fallback: if a fragment is evicted between batch assembly and execution, runtime falls back to on-the-fly materialization without failing the request
All new public configuration flags documented and gated behind runtime-1.21 feature flag
implementation_notes: Fragment fingerprinting: canonicalize fragment bytes (normalize separator tokens), compute SHA256 and truncate to 128 bits for index keys
Fragment size heuristics: prefer 128B-8KB fragments; allow configuration for experimental ranges
GPU storage layout: allocate large pinned allocations and sub-allocate fixed-size pages for fragments to avoid fragmentation; store pointer table in GPU memory for O(1) mapping
Indexing: CPU side bloom filters + LRU hashmap for exact fingerprint->GPU pointer resolution; use lock-free reads for hot path
Reference semantics: maintain atomic soft_ref_count (32-bit) and epoch-based last_used to inform eviction; soft refs do not prevent immediate eviction but bump eviction priority
Batch-aware eviction: during batch assembly, mark fragments as in-use; eviction threads must defer freeing pages until outstanding batch execution completes
Zero-copy batch assembly: batcher composes request KV by reading pointer table and emitting references to GPU kernels rather than copying raw bytes
Fallback path: if a requested fragment is missing or moved, fall back to the existing materialize-and-copy path and record a telemetry event
Compatibility: provide toggle to keep per-request copy behavior for debugging and canarying
Metrics: fragment_store.hits/misses, bloom.false_positives, eviction.bytes_freed, fragment.ref_count_distribution, fragment.lifetime_seconds
benchmarks: Target reduction in duplicate KV memory: >=60% on dev traffic trace A (combined chat+code)
Expected throughput increase: +10-20% requests/sec for batching-heavy workloads due to reduced memcpy overhead
Tail-latency target: P99 latency regression <= +1ms vs baseline with feature turned on
Memory compaction target: reduce peak GPU KV footprint by at least 28% on average customer traces
Index lookup budget: CPU bloom-filter + hashmap lookup should add <= 50 microseconds median overhead to batch assembly path
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime-1.21 and runtime.kv.fragment_store.enable flag
Internal canary: enable for internal-only traffic and synthetic high-share workloads for 48h
Gradual ramp: 1% customer traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 2-3 weeks with monitoring gates
Automated rollback: if fragment_store.hits drops or bloom.false_positives spike causing latency > +1ms at P99, rollback the flag automatically
Post-rollout: collect 30-day retention of fragment store metrics and artifactized sample of evicted fragments for offline analysis
migration_strategy: No customer-visible state changes required; store lives in runtime ephemeral GPU + CPU indexes
For Dedicated/Private deployments, document memory knobs and default thresholds; require operator restart for initial allocation sizing
Provide tooling to snapshot fingerprint stats and import/export bloom filters for pre-warming in Private/VPC installs
Backfill: run an opt-in pre-warm job that scans recent prompt traces and populates the fragment store on startup for high-share tenants
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint normalization and collision handling
Integration tests that exercise batch assembly with canonical fragment mapping and fallback materialization
Chaos tests: simulate concurrent eviction during batch assembly to validate graceful fallback
End-to-end perf tests measured against production-like traces (chat, embeddings, code completion)
GPU stress test to validate allocator behavior under fragmentation and eviction pressure
A/B experiment in canary cohort measuring customer-visible latency and throughput
